model_status.statement: One run, no seed on file, no persistence baseline, no evaluation record. Its error figure has nothing to be compared against.
The headline F1 used a threshold tuned on the rows it is scored on. The event-level evaluation exists as code and config but has no result on file.
Scored worse than the rule baseline (mean PUE change below zero), and is quarantined.
Scored once under the physics-1 protocol: outcome C, claim allowed: none. A fixed setting scored higher than every seed. Not promoted.
reports/policy_evaluation_physics1/full_0fcafef9d28fd539/ (outcome C). The older legacy-physics report is baselines-only (NOT_EVALUATED).

items.text: Every model in this system (forecaster, anomaly detector, PPO optimizer) is trained on data generated by src.data_generator/DigitalTwin itself — the same physics model the product simulates, not measurements from a real facility. This means:
Metrics (F1, RMSE, PUE improvement) measure how well each model fits the simulator's own physics/patterns, not real-world generalization.
Any systematic gap between the simulator and a real facility (thermal time constants, sensor noise characteristics, failure modes) is invisible to these numbers by construction.
Real historical data-centre datasets (public PUE benchmarks, or a partner facility) are needed to calibrate the physics and validate these models against reality, not just internal consistency.
Report these metrics as "performance on the current simulator," not as a claim about real-facility performance, until real data closes this gap.

sections.title: Synthetic training data (applies to all three models)

items.text: No carbon data file ships; the twin uses a flat assumed intensity, labelled as such (docs/model_cards/DATA_TRUTH.md). Carbon figures and anything optimised against them are not grid measurements.
items.title: Carbon is an assumption.

items.text: The promoted forecaster and anomaly detector, and the legacy PPO, were trained under physics legacy-0 whose parameters were not recorded; the v2 PPO candidates use physics 1. Two registry entries still carry a named compatibility waiver, and no re-validation record is on file.
items.title: Physics versions differ.

items.text: In both runs a fixed setting beat it on reward and water, so "better than the rule baseline" is a low bar. In the older legacy-physics run no policy kept the inlet temperature above its simulated minimum; under physics 1 the hard-limit counters are zero for the rule, the best constant and every PPO seed.
items.title: The rule baseline is weak.

items.text: The model is a lumped thermal and energy simulator with published parameters, not fitted to any facility (docs/PHYSICS_V2.md). Nothing here is a measurement.
items.title: Simulated, lumped, uncalibrated.

items.text: Sample sizes are small (3 seeds for the legacy PPO, one run for the other two) and the stated interval for the legacy PPO uses a multiplier that is too small for 3 seeds.
items.title: No uncertainty is shipped.

items.text: The training data file is not shipped; the registry holds its SHA-256, not the data.
items.title: Not reproducible from this repository alone.
